To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NAD (P), a cofactor for over 500 enzymes, is a promising target for drug discovery.

the NAD-binding domain of NAD(P)-dependent enzymes is much more diversified than previously thought, that the NAD mimics are highly potent and efficient inhibitors of NAD(P) dependent enzymes, that NAD mimicking inhibitors of NAD ligases, NAD kinases, NMN adenylyl transferases and phosphoribosiltransferases are on the horizon, and that the NAD binding domain is a highly selective and promising target for therapeutic intervention.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of NAD mimics as potential therapeutics.
the discovery and development of novel NAD (P), NADH, and NADPH based therapeutic agents, and with their use for the development of novel therapeutics.
the discovery and development of NAD (p) mimics and their use as potential therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NAD-based therapeutics is on the verge of a new era.
NAD mimicking therapeutics are here to stay and will be of great value to mankind in the years to come.
the field of NAD-based therapeutics is booming and that it is likely that the first NAD-based drugs would be approved in a not too distant future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been successful in developing a new class of NAD (NADP)-mimetics that can be used for the design of potent inhibitors of NAD(P)-dependent enzymes.
the NAD binding domain is much more diverse than previously thought and it has been possible to design inhibitors with high selectivity for a given NAD (P ) dependent enzymes.
the field of NAD (NADP) based therapeutic is rapidly expanding and the future looks very promising.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the NAD-binding domain in NAD(P)-dependent enzymes is much more diversified than previously thought and this is reflected by a large number of highly potent and selective NAD mimics that have been reported.
the NAD-binding domain is a highly druggable target and that it is possible to design highly selective inhibitors of this domain.
NAD (P )-based therapies are not a chimera anymore, but a reality.
